# E8 — Bio page

**Milestone:** M3 · **Depends on:** E5, E6 · **Unblocks:** E9

**Goal:** the public bio page at `juano.posta.lat/`, statically generated by Next, CDN-served, unfurling cleanly — plus the editor whose live preview **is the page component**.

**Done when:** the page scores well on mobile from a LATAM connection, unfurls correctly in WhatsApp and Instagram, and editing the bio updates the live page within seconds.

> **Amended invariant 11** [INV-11]: bio and dashboard are one frontend surface. See spec §11. This epic is materially smaller than originally planned because the `contracts/themes` indirection was deleted — themes are React components.

---

## S8.1 — Public bio page

**As a** visitor from Instagram **I want** a fast mobile page **so that** the first thing I see of Posta is not a spinner.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Route in `apps/web` resolving the handle from the host, rendering the bio [INV-11]
- [ ] **Statically generated with on-demand revalidation** — not request-time SSR
- [ ] Mobile-first; the desktop treatment is secondary
- [ ] Always-dark terminal theme regardless of visitor preference (DESIGN.md §1)
- [ ] Avatar with lime ring, `@handle` mono, display name, bio
- [ ] Vertical stack of terminal-styled link buttons: lime `→` cursor, hover lifts border to lime + `translateY`
- [ ] Subtle background grid; mono footer `hecho con Posta`
- [ ] Links point at the **short link** (`juano.posta.lat/<slug>`) so every bio click is tracked [thesis]
- [ ] Unknown handle → the on-brand 404
- [ ] Hit targets ≥44px [a11y]
- [ ] No cookies, no client analytics, no third-party requests [INV-6]

**Tasks:**
- [ ] T8.1.1 handle-from-host route resolution
- [ ] T8.1.2 `generateStaticParams` + ISR config
- [ ] T8.1.3 page composition from E6 primitives
- [ ] T8.1.4 terminal link buttons with hover states
- [ ] T8.1.5 background grid + footer
- [ ] T8.1.6 404 for unknown handle
- [ ] T8.1.7 test: zero third-party requests and zero cookies [INV-6]
- [ ] T8.1.8 Lighthouse mobile budget in CI

> The bio links go through the shortener rather than straight to the destination. That is what makes "every bio link is already tracked" true, and it is the reason `bio_links` references `links.id` back in S1.1.

## S8.2 — OG tags & unfurling

**As a** user sharing my bio **I want** it to preview properly **so that** the link looks credible in a DM.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] `generateMetadata` produces title, description, `og:*`, `twitter:*`
- [ ] OG image per handle — statically generated, cached, with avatar + name + handle
- [ ] Correct absolute URLs, driven by `POSTA_LINK_DOMAIN`
- [ ] `og:image` dimensions and type declared so clients render it immediately
- [ ] Verified in WhatsApp, Instagram DM, Telegram, X and Slack — **manually, on real devices**
- [ ] Missing avatar falls back to a generated monogram rather than a broken image

**Tasks:**
- [ ] T8.2.1 `generateMetadata` per handle
- [ ] T8.2.2 OG image generation (`next/og`)
- [ ] T8.2.3 absolute URL construction from env
- [ ] T8.2.4 monogram fallback
- [ ] T8.2.5 real-device unfurl verification, recorded

> Unfurler traffic hitting the *bio* page is itself a demonstration of the thesis. It is worth screenshotting the receipts for the build-in-public post.

## S8.3 — Themes

**As a** user **I want** two or three terminal themes **so that** the page feels like mine.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] 2–3 themes as React components/variants sharing one prop contract
- [ ] All are terminal-flavoured and stay dark (DESIGN.md §1)
- [ ] Theme id persisted on `bio_pages`; unknown/removed id falls back to default rather than crashing the public page
- [ ] Adding a theme is one file plus one registry entry
- [ ] Each theme passes contrast checks [a11y]

**Tasks:**
- [ ] T8.3.1 theme prop contract + registry
- [ ] T8.3.2 default theme
- [ ] T8.3.3 two variants
- [ ] T8.3.4 unknown-id fallback
- [ ] T8.3.5 contrast checks [a11y]

## S8.4 — Bio editor (`/bio`)

**As a** user **I want** to edit my page and see it live **so that** I am not publishing blind.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Split view: form left, live mobile preview right; **stacked on mobile** (form above preview)
- [ ] Form: avatar upload, nombre, bio, theme picker, ordered link list
- [ ] Links are **picked from existing short links** — no free-text URLs, so everything stays tracked [thesis]
- [ ] Add/remove; reorder with up/down arrow buttons (no drag library)
- [ ] **The preview renders the real page component** [INV-11] — not a lookalike
- [ ] Preview updates as you type
- [ ] Lime **Guardar**; toast `bio guardada`
- [ ] Unsaved-changes guard on navigation
- [ ] Reorder buttons are keyboard-operable and announce position changes [a11y]

**Tasks:**
- [ ] T8.4.1 split layout, responsive stack
- [ ] T8.4.2 form fields + validation from `contracts`
- [ ] T8.4.3 link picker over existing links
- [ ] T8.4.4 up/down reordering with position persistence
- [ ] T8.4.5 preview mounting the real page component [INV-11]
- [ ] T8.4.6 save + toast
- [ ] T8.4.7 unsaved guard
- [ ] T8.4.8 keyboard reordering + announcements [a11y]

> The preview being the real component is the entire payoff of the amended invariant. If it ever becomes "a simplified preview for performance", drift is back and the invariant bought nothing.

## S8.5 — Avatar upload

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] Upload to R2 via a **presigned URL** — the file never proxies through the API
- [ ] Accept jpg/png/webp only, validated by **magic bytes, not extension or client MIME** [security]
- [ ] Max 2 MB, enforced server-side [security]
- [ ] Resized/normalised to a square before storage
- [ ] Stored under a tenant-scoped, non-guessable key [INV-9]
- [ ] Served from a CDN-cached public URL
- [ ] Replacing an avatar cleans up the old object
- [ ] Upload failure has a clear Spanish error and does not corrupt existing state
- [ ] SVG is rejected outright [security]

**Tasks:**
- [ ] T8.5.1 presigned upload endpoint, tenant-scoped
- [ ] T8.5.2 magic-byte validation [security]
- [ ] T8.5.3 size cap server-side [security]
- [ ] T8.5.4 square normalisation
- [ ] T8.5.5 old-object cleanup
- [ ] T8.5.6 error states
- [ ] T8.5.7 hostile-upload tests: SVG, polyglot, oversized, wrong magic bytes [security]

> SVG is an XSS vector when served from your own origin. Reject it rather than sanitising it.

## S8.6 — Revalidation & routing proof

**As an** operator **I want** saves to publish quickly and the path split to demonstrably work **so that** the amended invariant holds in production, not just in theory.

**Acceptance:**
- [ ] On bio save, the API calls Next's on-demand revalidation webhook for that handle
- [ ] The webhook is authenticated with a shared secret [security]
- [ ] Revalidation failure is logged and alerted — the page silently serving stale content is the failure mode to catch
- [ ] Save → live page updated within seconds, asserted in an E2E test
- [ ] **Routing proof:** an E2E test against the real domain asserting `juano.posta.lat/` serves the bio and `juano.posta.lat/<slug>` 307s [INV-11]
- [ ] The same test asserts `/:slug` did **not** touch Next — the Origin Rule must not be over-matching
- [ ] **Revalidation reaches every replica**, not just the pod that received the webhook [INV-11]
- [ ] A fan-out test proves a save is visible from every `web` replica, not from a single sampled one

**Tasks:**
- [ ] T8.6.1 revalidation webhook with secret auth [security]
- [ ] T8.6.2 API call on bio save
- [ ] T8.6.3 failure logging + alert
- [ ] T8.6.4 E2E: save → live update
- [ ] T8.6.5 E2E: path-split proof on the real domain [INV-11]

> The Origin Rule is configuration living outside the repo, which makes it the most likely thing to be silently wrong after a Cloudflare change. T8.6.5 is the tripwire — it is also why E10 keeps it in the post-deploy smoke suite.

> **Multi-replica ISR breaks this invariant silently, and it is not obvious.** Next's default incremental cache is the pod's own filesystem. Under Kubernetes with more than one `web` replica, the revalidation webhook invalidates **only the pod that happens to receive it**; every other replica keeps serving the old bio indefinitely — at 200, fast, with nothing in any log. The user sees "I saved it and it didn't update… sometimes", which is close to unfalsifiable from the outside.
>
> The fix is a shared `cacheHandler` backed by Redis, so invalidation is cluster-wide (E10/S10.4). The test has to assert the save is visible from **every** replica: sampling one replica passes roughly `1/n` of the time by luck and is worse than no test, because it manufactures confidence.
>
> Found while writing E10, not E8 — the failure only exists once there is more than one replica, which is exactly why it would have reached production.
